review_notes: 4 rounds. R1 FIX-BEFORE-MERGE: 3 HIGH in the new canonical writer (sync_article returns False rather than raising, so failures were swallowed; non-atomic write of 15MB feed.json; replacements applied sequentially so one could consume another's output) + 4 MEDIUM. R2 FAIL: 2 blocking (a missing next SPY session stored None and let mean() shrink the denominator behind the fail-loud invariant; the lookahead test only observed the SPY download). R3: blocking 1 CLOSED, blocking 2 left one gap (recorder aborted on call 3, so a future 4th download was unobservable). R4 PASS: gap closed via a deferred tripwire; verified .columns is the first attribute main() touches and only _StopEarly is caught. Every fix was mutation-tested locally: restoring the proxy turns 5 tests red, reverting the exclusive `end` turns the lookahead test red, mutating only ^VIX's end is caught, and adding a 4th download (^TNX, end=2026-07-31) turns all 3 lookahead tests red. No fix after R1 changed any number: the 13-row table and all 8 summary statistics are byte-identical across R2/R3/R4.
review_caveats: R2/R3/R4 ran in a read-only sandbox with no writable tmpdir, so the reviewer could not execute pytest. Verdicts are based on line-by-line control-flow analysis, commit diffs and git blob equality. All pass/fail counts (55 passed) and every mutation test were run locally by the author, not by the reviewer.
Out of scope and NOT reviewed: k528 uses the same first-Friday proxy (20.9% of its 254 dates are wrong) and the live article's headline statistics derive from it. See report section 7.
